newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-TOP HORSES DECLARED FOR ARC.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-TOP HORSES DECLARED FOR ARC.

text.p: All the leading horses for Sunday's
Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe were among Friday's final
declarations.
Sixteeen runners will face the Longchamp starter after
English entry Luso and French five-year-old Sunshack, both
outsiders, dropped out overnight.
With a medium-sized field the draw should not influence the
outcome greatly, although those positioned in the centre are
thought to have a slight advantage.
Helissio, 5-2 favourite to keep the Arc and the $825,000
first prize at home in France was drawn five, which should not
prove a great incovenience.
Second favourite Zagreb (5-1), Irish Derby winner and mount
of Michael Kinane, is less favourably treated in stall three,
while Swain (11-2), third in the race last year, is on the other
side at 13.
English-trained raiders Pentire (8-1) and Classic Cliche
(also 8-1), mount of Frankie Dettori, seem fairly well placed at
seven and 12 respectively.
Epsom Derby winner Shaamit is in stall six, not a great
problem for jockey Pat Eddery who has won the Arc four times
previously.
The going at Longchamp is currently classified as very soft,
although it has improved of late. But showers are forecast over
the next two days and an easy surface looks assured for Sunday's
race, the richest in Europe.
The Arc is the highlight of a two-day festival of racing
which starts on Saturday with an attractive card featuring the
French version of the stayers' championship, the group one Prix
du Cadran.
English horses Double Trigger and Moonax clash with leading
French hope Kassani, owned by the Aga Khan.
